prompts.q: Name one of the five signs scored in the Apgar score (Virginia Apgar, 1952)
prompts.note: Each scored 0 to 2 at 1 and 5 minutes after birth. The letters were later back-fitted to spell APGAR.

prompts.q: Name a primitive (newborn) reflex
prompts.note: Present at or soon after birth and normally fading in the first months as the cortex matures.

prompts.q: Name one of Erik Erikson's eight stages of psychosocial development
prompts.note: Each stage is a crisis between two poles, from infancy (trust vs mistrust) to old age (integrity vs despair).

prompts.q: Name a neurotransmitter
prompts.note: Classic small-molecule transmitters plus a few well-known neuropeptides and gases.

prompts.q: Name a structure of the basal ganglia
prompts.note: Usually listed: striatum (caudate + putamen), globus pallidus, subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra, plus the ventral striatum.

prompts.q: Name a winner of the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine from 1931 to 1939
prompts.note: 1931 Warburg; 1932 Sherrington, Adrian; 1933 Morgan; 1934 Whipple, Minot, Murphy; 1935 Spemann; 1936 Dale, Loewi; 1937 Szent-Györgyi; 1938 Heymans; 1939 Domagk.

prompts.q: Name a part of the airway air passes through, from the nostrils to the alveoli
prompts.note: Conducting zone (nose to terminal bronchioles), then the respiratory zone where gas exchange starts.

prompts.q: Name a muscle of the soft palate or pharynx
prompts.note: Five soft-palate muscles and six pharyngeal muscles (three constrictors, three longitudinal).

prompts.q: Name a measurement from lung function testing
prompts.note: Spirometry, lung volumes and gas transfer, as reported on a standard full lung function test.

prompts.q: Name a part of the eye
prompts.note: Globe, its layers and fluids; eyelids and tear glands are adnexa, so not on the list.

prompts.q: Name a leading cause of blindness or vision impairment worldwide (WHO World Report on Vision, 2019)
prompts.note: The report's main causes. Uncorrected refractive error and cataract cause most vision impairment; much of it is preventable or treatable.

prompts.q: Name a human sense (beyond the classic five too)
prompts.note: Aristotle's five plus the senses physiologists now add.

prompts.q: Name an infection or illness people can catch from birds
prompts.note: Directly or via droppings, eggs, meat or mosquitoes that feed on birds.

prompts.q: Name a medical sign or term named after a bird
prompts.note: From the ward round to the radiology report.

prompts.q: Name an antiviral medicine
prompts.note: Approved antivirals for flu, herpes, COVID-19, hepatitis and HIV.

prompts.q: Name a wave, interval or segment on an ECG
prompts.note: The standard waveform features of a normal 12-lead trace.

prompts.q: Name a heart rhythm or arrhythmia
prompts.note: Normal rhythms plus the arrhythmias you'd see on a monitor.

prompts.q: Name a cause of hearing loss
prompts.note: Conductive, sensorineural or mixed.

prompts.q: Name a type of shock
prompts.note: Shock is circulatory failure; types are grouped by cause.

prompts.q: Name a part of a neuron
prompts.note: The nerve cell and the parts that let it send a signal.

prompts.q: Name a carpal bone
prompts.note: Proximal row: scaphoid, lunate (moon-shaped), triquetrum, pisiform. Distal row: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

prompts.q: Name a feature of Cushing's syndrome
prompts.note: Signs and symptoms of long-term high cortisol, from moon face to thin skin.

prompts.q: Name a medical imaging method
prompts.note: Ways of seeing inside the body, from X-rays to nuclear medicine.

prompts.q: Stephen Hawking's birthday: name a neurodegenerative disease
prompts.note: Diseases in which nerve cells progressively die. Hawking had motor neurone disease (ALS) for 55 years.

prompts.q: Name a sign of an upper or lower motor neurone lesion
prompts.note: MND is unusual in giving both kinds at once.

prompts.q: Name a type of oxygen or breathing support
prompts.note: From nasal prongs to life support.

prompts.q: iPhone unveiled (2007): name a health problem linked to phone or screen use
prompts.note: Problems blamed on heavy smartphone use; evidence is stronger for some than others.

prompts.q: Name a muscle that moves the thumb
prompts.note: Four extrinsic forearm muscles and the thenar and adductor muscles of the hand.

prompts.q: Name a health measurement a smartwatch or fitness tracker can make
prompts.note: Features on current consumer wearables (not all are medical-grade).

prompts.q: First UN General Assembly (1946): name one of the eight Millennium Development Goals (2000)
a: Combat HIV/AIDS, malaria and other diseases
prompts.note: The UN's 2000 to 2015 goals, replaced by the 17 Sustainable Development Goals.

prompts.q: Name a UN agency or programme that works on health
a: International Agency for Research on Cancer
International Agency for Research on Cancer
United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
United Nations Office for Project Services
prompts.note: UN system bodies with a health role, including WHO's specialised cancer agency.

prompts.q: Name a Director-General of the World Health Organization (1948 to now)
prompts.note: Brock Chisholm, Marcolino Candau, Halfdan Mahler, Hiroshi Nakajima, Gro Harlem Brundtland, Lee Jong-wook, Margaret Chan and Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (plus acting DG Anders Nordström, 2006-07).

prompts.q: First insulin injection (1922): name a symptom of high blood sugar
prompts.note: Classic symptoms of hyperglycaemia and undiagnosed diabetes.

prompts.q: Name a medicine used to treat type 2 diabetes
prompts.note: Tablets and injections; insulin itself counts.

prompts.q: Name an insulin (generic or brand)
prompts.note: Rapid, short, intermediate, long-acting and premixed insulins.

prompts.q: Charles Perrault's birthday: name a syndrome named after a story, myth or fictional character
prompts.note: Medicine borrows freely from literature and legend.

prompts.q: Name a sleep disorder
prompts.note: Including Sleeping Beauty's real-life namesake, Kleine-Levin syndrome.

prompts.q: Name a part of the foot (for Cinderella's slipper)
prompts.note: Surface parts and the bones and soft tissue underneath.

prompts.q: Rubber Ducky Day: name a waterborne disease
prompts.note: Infections caught from drinking, swimming or washing in contaminated water.

prompts.q: Name a medical item traditionally made from rubber or latex
prompts.note: Many are now latex-free because of latex allergy.

prompts.q: Name a condition with 'water' in its everyday name
prompts.note: The plain-English names patients use.

prompts.q: Name a duct in the body
prompts.note: Duck, duct: close enough.

prompts.q: Name something in medicine that's yellow (or named for being yellow)
prompts.note: Rubber ducks are yellow. So is a lot of medicine.

prompts.q: Albert Schweitzer's birthday: name a qualified doctor who became famous for something else
prompts.note: Schweitzer was a doctor, organist, theologian and Nobel Peace laureate.

prompts.q: Name a medical charity or humanitarian health organisation
a: International Committee of the Red Cross
International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
Royal Flying Doctor Service of Australia
The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
prompts.note: Non-government groups that deliver or fund health care.

prompts.q: Name a tropical disease spread by a fly (not a mosquito)
prompts.note: Tsetse flies, blackflies, sandflies, deerflies and house flies all carry disease.

prompts.q: Wikipedia Day: name a famous medical reference book or textbook
a: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology
Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
Goodman & Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics
prompts.note: Classic references, from Avicenna to the junior doctor's pocket.

prompts.q: Name an eponymous sign of appendicitis or the acute abdomen
prompts.note: Named signs from the surgical examination.

prompts.q: Name a medical specialty or science ending in -ology
prompts.note: Specialties, sub-specialties and lab sciences.

prompts.q: Prohibition ratified (1919): name a long-term health effect of heavy drinking
prompts.note: Harms from years of heavy alcohol use.

prompts.q: Name a medicine used for alcohol dependence or withdrawal
prompts.note: Withdrawal management, relapse prevention and vitamin replacement.

prompts.q: Name a chemical that is an alcohol (has an -OH group)
prompts.note: Drinking alcohol is just one: ethanol. Glycols, sugar alcohols and even cholesterol count too.

prompts.q: Benjamin Franklin's birthday (inventor of bifocals): name a way to correct vision
prompts.note: Lenses, contact lenses and surgery.

prompts.q: Name a trigger of gout (Franklin suffered from it)
prompts.note: Things that raise uric acid or set off a gout attack.

prompts.q: Name a feature of lead poisoning (Franklin warned about lead in 1786)
prompts.note: Signs and symptoms of high blood lead in adults and children.

prompts.q: Thesaurus Day: name another word or phrase for vomiting
prompts.note: From the clinical to the colourful.

prompts.q: Name an everyday word for the stomach or belly
prompts.note: Tummy talk.

prompts.q: Name a word for feeling unwell
prompts.note: How patients say they feel.

prompts.q: Edgar Allan Poe's birthday (his wife died of TB): name a symptom of tuberculosis
prompts.note: Classic symptoms of active lung TB.

prompts.q: Name a sign doctors use to confirm death (Poe feared being buried alive)
prompts.note: Bedside signs of death and the changes that follow.

prompts.q: Name a sound a doctor might hear through a stethoscope
prompts.note: Heart, lung, bowel and blood vessel sounds (The Tell-Tale Heart, anyone?).

prompts.q: Penguin Awareness Day: name a cold injury or cold-related illness
prompts.note: What the cold can do to people (penguins are better insulated).

prompts.q: Name a type of abnormal walk (gait)
prompts.note: Penguins waddle. So do people with weak hip muscles.

prompts.q: Name a medicine usually stored in the fridge
prompts.note: Medicines kept at 2 to 8°C until opened or used.

prompts.q: Name a seafood that can make people ill when eaten
prompts.note: Toxins, allergies aside: what fish and shellfish can do.

prompts.q: Name a medical sign or condition with snow or ice in its name
prompts.note: From snowflake cataracts to ice-pick headaches.

prompts.q: National Hugging Day: name a hormone made by the hypothalamus
prompts.note: Oxytocin, the 'cuddle hormone', is made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

prompts.q: Name a muscle you use to give a hug (chest, shoulder or arm)
prompts.note: Big hugs need the chest, shoulder girdle and arm muscles.

prompts.q: Name a touch receptor or nerve ending in the skin
prompts.note: Mechanoreceptors and other endings that tell you you've been hugged.

prompts.q: Francis Bacon's birthday (father of the scientific method): name a type of research study
prompts.note: Study designs, from case reports to meta-analyses.

prompts.q: Name a type of bias or error in medical research
prompts.note: The ways results can mislead.

prompts.q: Name a germ that causes pneumonia (Bacon died of it in 1626)
prompts.note: Bacteria, viruses and fungi behind community and hospital pneumonia.

prompts.q: First US woman to earn a medical degree (Elizabeth Blackwell, 1849): name a pioneering woman in medical history
prompts.note: Doctors, nurses and scientists who broke ground.

prompts.q: Name a US Ivy League university with a medical school
a: Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons
Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania
prompts.note: Seven of the eight Ivies have one; Princeton doesn't.

prompts.q: Name an obstetric emergency
prompts.note: Emergencies in pregnancy, labour and soon after birth.

prompts.q: Moebius Syndrome Awareness Day: name a cause of facial nerve palsy
prompts.note: Moebius syndrome is a rare congenital palsy of the facial (VII) and abducens (VI) nerves.

prompts.q: International Day of Education: name a level of Bloom's taxonomy (original or revised)
prompts.note: Original (1956): knowledge, comprehension, application, analysis, synthesis, evaluation. Revised (2001): remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create.

prompts.q: Burns Night: name a type or depth of burn
prompts.note: Burns are classed by cause and by depth.

prompts.q: Name a first aid step for a burn
prompts.note: Australian first aid advice for burns and scalds.

prompts.q: Name an organ eaten as offal (haggis has heart, liver and lungs)
prompts.note: Organ meats around the world.

prompts.q: Kawasaki Disease Awareness Day: name a feature of Kawasaki disease
prompts.note: Fever for 5+ days plus some of the classic signs; the big risk is coronary artery aneurysm.

prompts.q: International Day of Clean Energy: name a health harm linked to air pollution
prompts.note: Effects of fine particles, ozone and other pollutants (WHO).

prompts.q: Name a medical sign or finding named after a food
prompts.note: Medicine's menu: fruit, veg, dairy and dessert.

prompts.q: Mozart's birthday (he had recurring sore throats): name a cause of a sore throat
prompts.note: Infections and other causes of pharyngitis.

prompts.q: Name a complication of a streptococcal infection
prompts.note: Group A strep can cause local, toxin and immune complications (one theory blames Mozart's death on strep).

prompts.q: Name a criterion in the Jones criteria for acute rheumatic fever
prompts.note: Major: carditis, arthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules. Minor: fever, arthralgia, raised ESR or CRP, prolonged PR interval.

prompts.q: Name a voice or vocal cord problem
prompts.note: Singers and talkers beware.

prompts.q: Name a type of hearing aid or hearing implant
prompts.note: Mozart could reportedly pick out a note at 7; hearing technology helps the rest of us.

prompts.q: Data Privacy Day: name a principle of medical ethics
prompts.note: Including the 'four principles' (Beauchamp and Childress) and confidentiality.

prompts.q: Name a notifiable disease in Australia
prompts.note: Diseases doctors or labs must report to public health (national list).

prompts.note: Conditions famous for looking like many other diseases.

a: Saint Louis University Mental Status Exam
prompts.note: Cognitive screening puzzles: draw a clock, recall words, name animals.

prompts.note: Primary and secondary headaches from the ICHD classification.

prompts.q: World NTD Day: name a medicine used to treat a neglected tropical disease
prompts.note: Mass drug administration and specific treatments for WHO's neglected tropical diseases.

prompts.q: Name a disease spread by mosquitoes
prompts.note: Anopheles, Aedes and Culex mosquitoes between them carry all of these.

prompts.q: Name an animal that can pass rabies (or Australian bat lyssavirus) to humans
prompts.note: Dogs cause almost all human rabies deaths worldwide.

prompts.q: World Leprosy Day: name a sign or complication of leprosy
prompts.note: Leprosy (Hansen's disease) damages skin and nerves; it is curable with multi-drug therapy.

prompts.q: Name a species of Mycobacterium
prompts.note: The genus behind TB, leprosy, Buruli ulcer and the fish tank granuloma.

prompts.q: Name a person or place linked to the history of leprosy
prompts.note: Carers, scientists, patients and former leprosaria.
